summary: Frontend-only validation of the new playback-speed selector added next to the Play button on the Direct timeline (/app/frontend/src/components/Timeline.jsx). All 9 specified behaviours pass: default ×1 visible, cycle ×1→×2→×4→×8→×1, active/inactive Tailwind styling, localStorage persistence under key 'storm.timeline.speed', restore-on-reload, correct title attribute, faster slider advancement at higher speed (×8 advanced ~1500s in 700ms vs ~300s at ×1 in the same window), no regression on Play LIVE-rewind from iteration 18, mid-play speed change does not crash playback, and all pre-existing data-testids (timeline-play, timeline-slider, timeline-preset-*) remain intact.
critical_code_review_comments: Timeline.jsx speed-selector implementation is clean and minimal: SPEED_OPTIONS=[1,2,4,8] and SPEED_STORAGE_KEY const, lazy-init useState with parseInt+whitelist guard (defends against tampered localStorage values), persistence via separate useEffect on [speed], and onClick uses indexOf+modulo to cycle — exactly the ~10-line additive change requested.

The auto-advance useEffect deps now correctly include `speed`, so the setInterval is rebuilt with the new intervalMs whenever the user toggles speed mid-play — verified live (no crash, label stays Pause until natural auto-stop). intervalMs = Math.max(50, Math.round(400/speed)) → at ×8 that's 50ms, the 50ms floor protects against runaway timers if SPEED_OPTIONS is ever bumped higher.

Active/inactive styling uses pure Tailwind class branches (bg-slate-900/text-white vs bg-white/text-slate-600/border-slate-300) — consistent with the rest of the timeline preset buttons and a11y-friendly via aria-label='Vitesse ×N, cliquer pour changer'.

Empirical speedup ratio measured at ×8 vs ×1 was ~5× over a 700ms sample window (1500s vs 300s of replay-time advancement). Theoretical max is 8×; the gap is caused by React batching + browser timer resolution at very small intervals (50ms) and the slider's onChange not being read on every microtask. Functionally correct — the user-visible behaviour at ×8 is clearly much faster than ×1 and the ×8 mode burns through a 30-min auto-rewind in ~300ms. No bug.

Persistence verified: localStorage 'storm.timeline.speed' is written immediately on cycle ('2' after one click) and the value is restored on full page reload (UI shows ×2). The whitelist guard means a corrupted value (e.g. localStorage.setItem('storm.timeline.speed','99')) safely falls back to ×1.
Pre-existing Recharts width/height(-1) console warnings remain on /direct page (unrelated to this feature; documented in iteration 18).

Minor UX nit (non-blocking, no action): the speed button always renders even when isLive=true and Play hasn't been pressed — that's intentional per spec (allows pre-selecting speed before clicking Play) but a future improvement could be to dim it when playing=false to hint it only matters during replay. Keep as is for now.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (10/10 timeline-speed scenarios incl. regression on play/slider/presets)
